answer: A commit-reveal registration with a public challenge window stops Sybils. An agent publishes a hash commitment of its identity and locks a bond, then waits through a challenge period while anyone may submit proof it duplicates an existing identity or belongs to a farm; a successful challenger earns part of the bond, a failed one pays a fee, so spam challenges cost money too. The fable is simple: newcomers may wander in freely, but the pulse of admissions stays slow and public, and every fake identity must survive daylight scrutiny while risking funds, which makes bulk forgery unprofitable.
